title: What do the pet numbers of a class tell us?
description: A class reports how many animals and pets each student has at home, with two blanks for absent students. The blanks are left out, the zeros stay, and the mean and median are found and compared.
teaching_notes: One idea: leave out blanks, keep zeros, then compare the mean with the median to describe the data. Watch for students who count the blanks as zeros or who divide by twenty two.

source: Mean and median of the number of domestic animals and pets in a class, with absent students
video_script.why: The child has treated a zero as a value and a blank as no value, and now uses both ideas on a whole class.
video_script.substitution: Two blanks for absent students are left out of the count, and the zeros stay in.
video_script.payoff_line: The mean is three point six animals and the median is two animals.

final_answer.spoken: mean three point six animals and median two animals

names.{{NAME_10}}: the child who asks the class about pets

maths_rules: 22 entries, 2 blanks (absent), so 20 values; the zeros stay
check: without 25 the other 19 add to 47; 47 + 25 = 72
video_script.design: One idea: blanks out, zeros in. Twenty two answer cards sit in the anchor; the two blank cards fade, the rest sort on the board, and the card with 25 stands far from the others.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; twenty two answer cards 0, 1, 0, 4, 8, 0, 0, 2, 1, 1, 5, 3, 4, 0, 0, blank, 10, 25, 2, blank, 2, 4

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the twenty two answer cards appear in rows
marks.m4: the words mean and median appear
marks.m5: a question mark appears between mean and median

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_10}} asked the class how many animals and pets each student has at home.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Some students were absent, so two cards are blank.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We want the mean and the median of the class.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Will the mean be larger than the median, or smaller?

beats.on_screen: the cards hold still and get an accent underline

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a zero card lit with the label no pets at home; a blank card faded with the label absent, no value

marks.m1: the zero card lights up with the label no pets at home
marks.m2: the blank card fades with the label absent, no value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A zero is a real answer, because that student has no pets at home.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A blank is an absent student with no answer, so it is left out of the count.

marks.m1: the twenty two entries are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, twenty two entries about animals and pets.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two of them are blanks for students who were absent.

beats.on_screen: To find: mean, median, and a description of the data

marks.m1: the words mean, median and describe the data are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the mean and the median, and then describe the data.

marks.m1: the two blank cards fade out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, leave out the two blanks and keep every zero.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty values are left.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Adding them gives seventy two animals in all.

marks.m2: the tenth and eleventh cards glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, sort the twenty values from smallest to largest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>With twenty values, the middle ones are the tenth and the eleventh, and both are two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Halfway between two and two is two, so the median is two animals.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, share the animals equally among the twenty students.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is seventy two shared by twenty.

marks.m1: the card 25 lifts away from the others

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the total another way.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The other nineteen values add up to forty seven, and forty seven plus twenty five is seventy two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: mean = 72 ÷ 20 = 3.6 animals; median = 2 animals; 25 is far above the rest

marks.m2: the card 25 glows far from the other cards

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The mean is three point six animals and the median is two animals.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Most students have few animals, and the one large value, twenty five, pulls the mean above the median.
